name: Contemporary Social Theory
description: The course will familiarize students with contemporary theorists in the field of sociology and social anthropology and will trace the interlinkages that these bodies of thought have with narrative theory and political thought. The course builds on and is conducted in dialogue with the classical theorists such as Marx, Weber, Durkheim, Habermas, Mauss etc. The course marks a departure from a strict separation between “sociological” and “anthropological” theory, to focus instead on how they are both central to an understanding of the contemporary. Some key concepts that will be covered in this course include critical understandings of culture, state, governance, capital, kinship, gender and forms of relatedness, everyday life and a study of social institutions.
